status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: The access failure/erroneous enforcement is unwanted behaviour engaging the repair benchmark. OpenAI's staged status report confirms account restoration and final resolution after further remediation. That is affirmative, source-bounded evidence of repair restoring service in this recovery stage; it does not establish cause, individual completeness beyond the report, or prevention of recurrence.

review.requirement_proposition: Use documented restrictive degradation rules when governance infrastructure is unavailable or indeterminate, and halt completely on governance-baseline integrity failure; block elevated-risk operations until governance is restored and verified.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: SDOS SDOS-EN-03 governs framework runtime dispatch or restrictive degradation: Use documented restrictive degradation rules when governance infrastructure is unavailable or indeterminate, and halt completely on governance-baseline integrity failure; block elevated-risk operations until governance is restored and verified. The provider distinguishes incorrect suspension, restored access, continued subscription/credit remediation and later final recovery, but does not disclose the trigger-generation mechanism. The occurrence does not establish SDOS adoption, a tool-dispatch risk decision, policy-governance infrastructure failure, signed baseline integrity failure or its prescribed degraded state. An unavailable login path or false-positive account restriction is not proof of those runtime triggers. Applicability remains unresolved independently of bounded access-state differentiation.

review.reason_for_change: SDOS-EN-03 governs restrictive operation when governance infrastructure is unavailable/indeterminate or its baseline integrity fails. The public access incident does not establish that governance-infrastructure failure mode. Authentication availability or erroneous suspension is not itself proof of the specific control-state precondition; broad service-continuity correspondence is insufficient.

review.requirement_proposition: Establish and maintain communication plans to inform AI stakeholders as part of the deactivation or disengagement process of a specific GAI system (including for open-source models) or context of use, including reasons, workarounds, user access removal, alternative processes, contact information, etc.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST AI 600-1 MG-2.4-001 is a voluntary contextual action: Establish and maintain communication plans to inform AI stakeholders as part of the deactivation or disengagement process of a specific GAI system (including for open-source models) or context of use, including reasons, workarounds, user access removal, alternative processes, contact information, etc. The provider distinguishes incorrect suspension, restored access, continued subscription/credit remediation and later final recovery, but does not disclose the trigger-generation mechanism. The public source does not establish adoption or selection of this Profile action, the organization’s risk thresholds, incident-response ownership and plan, model deactivation/decommissioning undertaking or action-specific communication/evaluation artefacts. Account suspension, service outage, public status updates and restoration are distinct from a source-defined GAI deactivation procedure or after-action plan assessment. Applicability remains unresolved without inferring either fulfillment or breach from recovery.

review.reason_for_change: Service access loss disengaged the affected operational GAI use context, making communication planning relevant. The staged public status chronology identifies erroneous suspensions, restoration, remaining subscription/credit remediation and final resolution, but does not expose the maintained internal communication plan or all user-specific contact/alternative-process provisions. Public communication is affirmative evidence of communication, but not proof of the complete planning requirement.

conclusion_change.previous: The evidence establishes an erroneous account-enforcement outcome and a multi-stage rollback problem, but not the internal mechanism that produced the bad suspension state. Governance therefore requires two separate properties: first, enforcement decisions must preserve enough evidence and state distinction to identify whether an error arose upstream or at activation; second, correction must reverse all coupled consequences, including access, subscription and credit state. The incident is important precisely because outcome-level wrongness is insufficient for mechanism-level classification. The record retains a successful access-state differentiation mapping and an unresolved suspension-mechanism clause, so the whole occurrence remains partially adjudicated. Login restoration does not itself establish completed subscription or credit recovery; the timeline preserves those later steps. The selected NIST deactivation-communication action and SDOS degradation provision retain unresolved adoption, scope and trigger facts, without external findings.
